NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Cloud Infrastructure / Senior Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior infrastructure and platform engineer with 10 years of experience, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure, infrastructure as code, and reliable platforms for product teams. Technical lead with a focus on self-service infrastructure, observable services, practical operational processes and measurable improvements to deployment speed and reliability.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure and operations: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), Kubernetes, Linux
Infrastructure as code and platform engineering: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Argo CD, Helm, Kustomize, Karpenter, Puppet
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Automation and testing: Go, Python, Bash, GitHub Actions, k6

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – Present
- Technical lead of a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform spanning eight clusters, approximately 350 services and three regions.
- Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane-based self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3; reduced the time to take a new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, reducing on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
- Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game-backend infrastructure across EC2, ECS and later EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code in Terraform across approximately 40 modules, using Atlantis for plan and apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Conducted pre-launch load testing with k6 and supported launch-day capacity planning.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational work with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021; renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from Linux systems engineering to senior platform leadership. The summary is concise and relevant, while the experience section uses credible scale and quantified outcomes: eight Kubernetes clusters, approximately 350 services, three regions, 60% fewer on-call pages, 38% lower EC2 spend, and a substantial reduction in service delivery time. The document is professional, readable, and appropriately focused on infrastructure and platform engineering. It also accurately reflects the Original Candidate Information; no potential hallucinated skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were detected. The main content limitation is that some capabilities relevant to this role—stakeholder alignment, systems architecture, networking security, and technical communication—are not explicitly evidenced, but the supplied candidate information does not provide enough support to add them as achievements.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, standard employment chronology, searchable technology names, and no apparent tables, graphics, columns, or parsing obstacles. It contains strong matches for AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, Linux, infrastructure as code, observability, reliability, and technical leadership. AI screening probability is high for the core AWS/platform-engineering portion of the role, but lower for the full specification because Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, security awareness, IoT or remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, and explicit system-design terminology are not present. These are candidate-experience gaps or unsupported areas rather than defects that can be fixed by inventing keywords.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with the hands-on infrastructure, AWS, Terraform, cloud operations, reliability, Linux, and technical-leadership aspects of the role. The Tallybrook role demonstrates ownership of a substantial platform, self-service infrastructure, GitOps, operational improvement, and incident processes—good evidence for Corvale's engineering-led, end-to-end ownership culture. The CV also shows practical scale and measurable outcomes relevant to building and operating production infrastructure. The candidate's material does not demonstrate Terragrunt, mutual TLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, practical security work, IoT/automotive/remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, or explicit stakeholder alignment with external engineering teams. These are genuine alignment gaps and should not be presented as document defects or addressed through unsupported additions.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ATS/alignment enhancement: In the Professional Summary section, revise the second sentence from "Experienced in designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure, infrastructure as code, and reliable platforms for product teams" to "Experienced in cloud environment design and operation, infrastructure as code, and building reliable platforms for product teams." This uses the job description's exact phrase while remaining supported by the documented AWS, EKS, Terraform, Crossplane, and platform-operations experience.
